questions.subject: Botany
questions.questionText: Which of the following was NOT among the five primary criteria used by R.H. Whittaker (1969) to establish the Five Kingdom Classification system?
options: A) Presence or absence of locomotory flagella
questions.explanation: Whittaker's Five Kingdom Classification was based on five major criteria: (1) cell structure (prokaryotic vs eukaryotic), (2) body organization (unicellular vs multicellular), (3) mode of nutrition (autotrophic vs heterotrophic), (4) reproduction, and (5) phylogenetic relationships. The presence or absence of flagella was not one of his primary classification criteria.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.questionText: Methanogens, an ancient group of archaebacteria responsible for the production of biogas (methane), are typically found in:
options: A) Hot sulfur springs with temperatures exceeding $80^\circ\text{C}$
B) The gut of several ruminant animals such as cows and buffaloes
C) Extreme hyper-saline inland salt lakes
D) The deep aphotic benthic zone of oceans
questions.explanation: Methanogens are obligate anaerobic archaebacteria found in the gut of several ruminant animals (cows, buffaloes) and in marshy areas, producing methane (biogas) from the dung of these animals. Thermoacidophiles inhabit hot sulfur springs (Option A), and halophiles thrive in extreme hyper-saline environments (Option B).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.questionText: Which of the following photosynthetic pigments is present in cyanobacteria (blue-green algae), conferring photosynthetic capability identical to higher green plants?
questions.explanation: Cyanobacteria possess chlorophyll a, which is identical to the primary photosynthetic pigment found in higher green plants, allowing them to carry out oxygenic photosynthesis. Fucoxanthin is characteristic of brown algae (Phaeophyceae) and diatoms.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.questionText: Specialized, thick-walled, pale cells found in cyanobacteria such as $\textit{Nostoc}$ and $\textit{Anabaena}$ that perform biological nitrogen fixation are called:
questions.explanation: Heterocysts are specialized non-photosynthetic, thick-walled cells in cyanobacteria ($\textit{Nostoc}$, $\textit{Anabaena}$) that lack oxygenic Photosystem II and contain nitrogenase, enabling biological nitrogen fixation under microaerophilic conditions. Akinetes are resting spores, and hormogonia are vegetative fragments.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.questionText: The cell walls of diatoms are uniquely indestructible and persist for millennia because they are embedded with:
questions.explanation: Diatom cell walls consist of two overlapping valves or shells that fit together like a soap box, heavily impregnated with amorphous hydrated silica (silicon dioxide). Because silica is chemically inert and indestructible, the accumulated cell walls form vast deposits known as 'diatomaceous earth'.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.questionText: Which organism is recognized as the causative agent of dangerous 'red tides' in coastal oceans through explosive population multiplication?
questions.explanation: $\textit{Gonyaulax}$ is a marine red dinoflagellate that undergoes such rapid population proliferation (blooms) that the sea appears red ('red tides'). They release potent neurotoxins (such as saxitoxin) that accumulate in marine food webs and cause massive fish mortality.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.questionText: Instead of a rigid cellulosic cell wall, euglenoids possess a flexible protein-rich outer covering termed the:
questions.explanation: Euglenoids lack a rigid cell wall; instead, they have a proteinaceous, flexible sub-membrane layer called the pellicle, which allows flexibility and shape changes (euglenoid movement). A capsid is a viral protein coat, a frustule is a diatom shell, and a theca is a dinoflagellate cellulosic armor.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.questionText: Under favorable environmental conditions, slime moulds aggregate to form a creeping, multinucleated mass of protoplasm termed a:
questions.explanation: Under suitable conditions of moisture and nutrients, acellular slime moulds aggregate into a multinucleate mass of protoplasm called a plasmodium, which may spread across several feet. During unfavorable conditions, the plasmodium differentiates into spore-bearing fruiting bodies.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.questionText: The cell walls of true fungi (Kingdom Fungi) are predominantly composed of:
questions.explanation: The cell walls of most fungi are composed of chitin (a polymer of N-acetylglucosamine) and complex polysaccharides (such as glucans). Peptidoglycan forms bacterial cell walls, and cellulose/pectin forms plant and green algal cell walls.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.questionText: In which class of fungi are asexual spores (conidia) produced EXOGENOUSLY, while sexual spores (ascospores) are produced ENDOGENOUSLY within sac-like structures?
questions.explanation: In Ascomycetes (sac fungi), asexual conidia are borne exogenously on the tips of specialized hyphae called conidiophores, whereas sexual ascospores are formed endogenously inside sac-like asci arranged within ascocarps.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.questionText: The common edible mushroom available in commercial vegetable markets, commonly known as button mushroom, belongs to the fungal genus:
questions.explanation: $\textit{Agaricus}$ (specifically $\textit{Agaricus bisporus}$) is the common edible button mushroom belonging to Class Basidiomycetes. $\textit{Rhizopus}$ is bread mould (Phycomycete), $\textit{Puccinia}$ is rust fungus (Basidiomycete), and $\textit{Ustilago}$ is smut fungus (Basidiomycete).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.questionText: Why is the fungal class Deuteromycetes commonly designated as the 'Imperfect Fungi'?
options: A) Their mycelium lacks cell walls entirely
B) They are obligate anaerobic parasites of vascular plants
C) They can reproduce only through motile biflagellate zoospores
D) Only their asexual or vegetative phases are known, while sexual stages are absent or undiscovered
questions.explanation: Deuteromycetes are called imperfect fungi because only their asexual or vegetative phases are known. When the sexual (perfect) stages of these fungi are discovered, they are moved into their rightful taxonomic classes, typically Ascomycetes or Basidiomycetes.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.questionText: Which scientist successfully crystallized the Tobacco Mosaic Virus (TMV) for the first time, demonstrating that virus crystals consist largely of proteins?
questions.explanation: W.M. Stanley in 1935 demonstrated that viruses could be crystallized and that these crystals consist largely of proteins. Dmitri Ivanowsky (1892) first recognized microbes causing mosaic disease; Beijerinek (1898) coined the term 'Contagium vivum fluidum'; and T.O. Diener (1971) discovered viroids.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.questionText: In a bacteriophage (a virus that infects bacterial cells), the genetic material is typically:
questions.explanation: Bacteriophages (viruses that infect bacteria) usually possess double-stranded DNA (dsDNA) as their genetic material. Plant viruses predominantly contain single-stranded RNA (ssRNA), and animal viruses may have single- or double-stranded RNA or double-stranded DNA.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.questionText: Viroids differ fundamentally from viruses in that viroids:
options: A) Possess a protein capsid but lack nucleic acid
B) Contain double-stranded DNA enclosed by a lipid envelope
C) Consist of free RNA of low molecular weight and completely lack a protein coat
D) Have a molecular weight vastly greater than infectious viral genomes
questions.explanation: Viroids, discovered by T.O. Diener in 1971, are infectious agents smaller than viruses consisting of a short strand of free, circular RNA of low molecular weight that completely lacks a protective protein coat (capsid).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.questionText: Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy (BSE), commonly called Mad Cow Disease, and its human variant Creutzfeldt-Jakob Disease (CJD), are caused by infectious agents termed:
questions.explanation: Prions are infectious neurological agents composed of abnormally folded proteins (lacking any nucleic acid) that induce fatal degenerative brain disorders such as BSE (Mad Cow Disease) in cattle and CJD in humans.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.questionText: Why are lichens widely recognized as excellent bioindicators of environmental air pollution?
options: A) They are extremely sensitive to pollutants like $\text{SO}_2$ and do not grow in polluted environments
B) They thrive in areas with high atmospheric sulfur dioxide concentration
C) They produce toxic volatile sulfur compounds when exposed to clean air
D) They exclusively grow on industrial waste effluents
questions.explanation: Lichens are exceptionally sensitive to air pollution, particularly sulfur dioxide ($\text{SO}_2$), because they absorb moisture and dissolved nutrients directly from the atmosphere without a protective cuticle. Consequently, they do not grow in polluted industrial regions and serve as natural pollution bioindicators.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.questionText: The algal component of a lichen is termed the ________, while the fungal component is termed the ________.
questions.explanation: In a lichen, the autotrophic algal partner is called the phycobiont (prepares food by photosynthesis), and the heterotrophic fungal partner is called the mycobiont (provides structural anchorage, absorbs water and mineral nutrients).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.questionText: Which organism lacks a cell wall, represents the smallest living cell known, and can survive entirely in the absence of oxygen?
questions.explanation: $\textit{Mycoplasma}$ (PPLO) completely lacks a cell wall, has a tiny diameter of approximately $0.3\;\mu\text{m}$, is capable of anaerobic survival, and causes pathogenic infections in both animals and plants.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.questionText: In Whittaker's Five Kingdom Classification, unicellular eukaryotic organisms like $\textit{Chlamydomonas}$, $\textit{Chlorella}$, and $\textit{Amoeba}$ are collectively placed in the Kingdom:
questions.explanation: Whittaker unified all unicellular eukaryotic organisms into Kingdom Protista. Consequently, $\textit{Chlamydomonas}$ and $\textit{Chlorella}$ (earlier placed under green algae in Kingdom Plantae) and $\textit{Amoeba}$ and $\textit{Paramecium}$ (earlier in Kingdom Animalia) are classified within Protista.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.questionText: Which fungal genus is extensively utilized as a primary model organism in biochemical and genetics research?
questions.explanation: $\textit{Neurospora crassa}$ (an Ascomycete fungus, often called the 'Drosophila of the plant kingdom') is widely used as a model organism in biochemical genetics (e.g., Beadle and Tatum's 'one gene-one enzyme' hypothesis).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.questionText: In the Three-Domain system proposed by Carl Woese, the six kingdoms are organized into three primary domains based on:
options: A) Number of chromosomes in somatic cells
B) 16S ribosomal RNA (rRNA) gene sequence and cellular membrane biochemistry
D) Ability to produce motile gametes
questions.explanation: Carl Woese established the Three-Domain system (Archaea, Bacteria, and Eukarya) primarily based on molecular phylogenetic analyses of 16S rRNA gene sequences and unique membrane lipid biochemistry (branched ether lipids in Archaea vs ester lipids in Bacteria and Eukarya).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Archaebacteria are capable of surviving under the most hostile and extreme environmental conditions, such as high salinity and boiling thermal vents.
Reason (R): Archaebacteria possess a distinct cell wall and cell membrane structure with ether-linked branched lipid chains that provide structural stability.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: A) (A) is true but (R) is false.
B) Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A).
C) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
D) (A) is false but (R) is true.
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is true: archaebacteria inhabit extreme habitats (halophiles in salt pans, thermoacidophiles in hydrothermal vents, methanogens in marshes). Reason (R) is true: NCERT explicitly notes that archaebacteria differ from eubacteria in having a different cell wall structure and a monolayer or branched-chain ether-linked lipid membrane that reduces membrane fluidity and prevents thermal degradation or osmotic lysis in extreme conditions. This biochemical difference is responsible for their survival; thus (R) correctly explains (A).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Euglenoids behave as photosynthetic autotrophs in the presence of sunlight, but become heterotrophic predators when deprived of sunlight.
Statement II: The photosynthetic pigments present in euglenoids are entirely different from those found in higher vascular plants.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
B) Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
C) Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
D) Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
questions.explanation: Statement I is correct: euglenoids exhibit mixotrophic nutrition; they are photosynthetic in light, but in the dark they predace upon smaller organisms like heterotrophs. Statement II is incorrect: NCERT explicitly states that the photosynthetic pigments of euglenoids (chlorophyll a and chlorophyll b) are identical to those of higher plants.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.questionText:
Match the fungal classes in Column I with their typical sexual/asexual spore characteristics in Column II:

Column I: (a) Phycomycetes, (b) Ascomycetes, (c) Basidiomycetes, (d) Deuteromycetes
Column II:
(i) Ascospores produced endogenously in asci
(ii) Basidiospores produced exogenously on basidia
(iii) Zygospores formed by fusion of gametangia; zoospores/aplanospores
(iv) Sexual reproduction absent or undiscovered; reproduce only by conidia

Select the correct matching combination:
questions.explanation: Phycomycetes produce zygospores sexually and zoospores/aplanospores asexually (a-iii); Ascomycetes form ascospores endogenously in asci (b-i); Basidiomycetes form basidiospores exogenously on basidia (c-ii); Deuteromycetes lack sexual spores and reproduce by asexual conidia (d-iv). Thus the correct matching sequence is (a)-(iii), (b)-(i), (c)-(ii), (d)-(iv).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.questionText: Which of the following statements regarding the structural features and biology of diatoms is INCORRECT?
options: A) Diatoms are microscopic and float passively in water currents as plankton.
B) The accumulation of diatom cell walls on ocean floors is easily degraded by marine saprophytic bacteria.
C) Diatoms are the chief 'producers' in the oceans.
D) The cell walls form two thin overlapping shells which fit together as in a soap box.
questions.explanation: Option D is incorrect: diatom cell walls are embedded with indestructible amorphous silica (silicon dioxide). When diatoms die, their walls accumulate over billions of years forming 'diatomaceous earth', which is not degraded by bacteria. Options A, B, and C are correct facts from NCERT.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Viruses are considered obligate intracellular parasites and are not included in Whittaker's Five Kingdom Classification.
Reason (R): Viruses lack cellular organization and remain completely inert crystalline entities outside a living host cell.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: A) (A) is true but (R) is false.
B) Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A).
C) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
D) (A) is false but (R) is true.
questions.explanation: Whittaker's Five Kingdom system classified organisms possessing cellular organization. Viruses, viroids, and prions are acellular (non-cellular) and do not have a cell membrane or independent cytoplasm. Outside a living host, viruses exist as inert, non-metabolizing nucleoprotein crystals. Once inside a host, they take over cellular machinery to replicate. Because they lack cellular organization and are inert outside hosts, they were excluded from cellular kingdoms. Thus (R) correctly explains (A).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.questionText:
Consider the following four statements regarding Kingdom Fungi:
(a) In Ascomycetes and Basidiomycetes, an intervening dikaryotic stage ($n+n$, i.e., two nuclei per cell) occurs before karyogamy.
(b) Fungi that absorb soluble organic matter from dead substrates are called saprophytes.
(c) The cell wall of fungi is composed of pure cellulose identical to green algae.
(d) Fungal sexual reproduction involves three successive steps: plasmogamy, karyogamy, and meiosis.

Which of the above statements are TRUE?
questions.explanation: Statements (a), (b), and (d) are true: Ascomycetes and Basidiomycetes show a distinct dikaryophase ($n+n$); fungi feeding on dead matter are saprophytes; and sexual reproduction proceeds via plasmogamy $\to$ karyogamy $\to$ meiosis. Statement (c) is false because fungal cell walls are composed of chitin and glucans (polysaccharides), not pure cellulose.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.questionText:
Match the diseases in Column I with their causative microorganisms in Column II:

Column I: (a) Citrus canker, (b) Potato spindle tuber disease, (c) Sleeping sickness, (d) Rust of wheat
Column II:
(i) $\textit{Puccinia graminis}$
(ii) $\textit{Xanthomonas axonopodis}$
(iii) Viroid
(iv) $\textit{Trypanosoma gambiense}$

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Citrus canker is caused by the bacterium $\textit{Xanthomonas}$ (a-ii); Potato spindle tuber disease is caused by a viroid (b-iii); Sleeping sickness is caused by the flagellated protozoan $\textit{Trypanosoma}$ (c-iv); Rust of wheat is caused by the basidiomycete fungus $\textit{Puccinia}$ (d-i). Thus the correct matching sequence is (a)-(ii), (b)-(iii), (c)-(iv), (d)-(i).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Chemosynthetic autotrophic bacteria play an essential role in recycling nutrients such as nitrogen, phosphorus, iron, and sulfur.
Statement II: Chemosynthetic autotrophic bacteria utilize radiant solar energy trapped by bacteriochlorophyll to synthesize ATP.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
B) Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
C) Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
D) Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
questions.explanation: Statement I is correct: chemosynthetic bacteria (such as $\textit{Nitrosomonas}$, $\textit{Nitrobacter}$, and sulfur-oxidizing bacteria) oxidize inorganic substrates and recycle key biogenic elements (N, P, Fe, S). Statement II is incorrect: chemosynthetic autotrophs do NOT use solar energy; instead, they oxidize inorganic substances (nitrates, nitrites, ammonia, hydrogen sulfide) and harness the released chemical energy to synthesize ATP.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.questionText: In which of the following groups of fungi are sex organs completely absent, but plasmogamy is accomplished by the fusion of two vegetative or somatic cells of different strains?
questions.explanation: In Basidiomycetes (club fungi), differentiated sex organs (antheridia and oogonia) are completely absent. Plasmogamy is achieved through somatogamy—the fusion of two vegetative or somatic cells belonging to different genetic strains or mating types, yielding a dikaryotic mycelium that produces basidia.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Slime mould spores possess remarkable resistance and can survive for several years under extremely harsh conditions.
Reason (R): Slime mould spores possess true cellulosic cell walls and are dispersed by air currents.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: A) (A) is false but (R) is true.
B) Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A).
C) (A) is true but (R) is false.
D) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is true: spores of slime moulds are extremely resistant and survive for years even under adverse conditions. Reason (R) is true: although the vegetative plasmodium lacks a cell wall, the differentiated spores possess true, tough cell walls that resist desiccation and temperature extremes, allowing them to be dispersed by air currents. The possession of true resistant walls explains their survival; hence (R) correctly explains (A).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.questionText:
Select the option that correctly matches the scientist with their milestone discovery in virology:

(1) Dmitri Ivanowsky (1892) — Crystallized Tobacco Mosaic Virus
(2) M.W. Beijerinek (1898) — Called the infectious living fluid '$\textit{Contagium vivum fluidum}'
(3) W.M. Stanley (1935) — Discovered viroids causing potato spindle tuber disease
(4) T.O. Diener (1971) — Demonstrated that viruses are smaller than bacteria using porcelain filters
questions.explanation: Only (2) is correctly matched: M.W. Beijerinek in 1898 demonstrated that the extract of infected tobacco leaves could transmit mosaic disease to healthy plants and termed the fluid '$\textit{Contagium vivum fluidum}$' (contagious living fluid). Ivanowsky (1892) showed they pass through bacteria-proof filters; Stanley (1935) crystallized TMV; and Diener (1971) discovered viroids.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.questionText: Coenocytic mycelium (a continuous tubular network filled with multinucleated cytoplasm without transverse septa) is a hallmark characteristic of which fungal group?
questions.explanation: In Phycomycetes (such as $\textit{Mucor}$, $\textit{Rhizopus}$, and $\textit{Albugo}$), the mycelium is aseptate and coenocytic (continuous tubes containing multinucleated cytoplasm). In contrast, Ascomycetes, Basidiomycetes, and Deuteromycetes possess branched, septate hyphae.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.questionText: Which of the following protozoans is actively moving, possesses a gullet (cavity) that opens to the outside of the cell surface, and coordinates thousands of cilia to steer food into its oral apparatus?
questions.explanation: $\textit{Paramecium}$ is a ciliated protozoan that is aquatic and actively moves via coordinated beating of thousands of cilia. It possesses a permanent oral groove leading to a gullet (cytopharynx); the rhythmic ciliary beating drives food-laden water currents into the gullet.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Morels and truffles are subterranean basidiocarps of puffball fungi, but are poisonous and inedible.
Statement II: $\textit{Neurospora}$ is an ascomycete fungus used extensively in biochemical and genetics research.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
B) Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
C) Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
D) Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
questions.explanation: Statement I is incorrect: morels and truffles belong to the class Ascomycetes (not puffballs or basidiomycetes) and are prized edible delicacies considered gastronomic luxuries. Statement II is correct: $\textit{Neurospora}$ is an Ascomycete fungus used worldwide as a central genetic model organism.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.questionText: Which of the following pairs of fungi belong to the Class Basidiomycetes and are well-known plant parasites causing 'rust' and 'smut' diseases respectively?
questions.explanation: $\textit{Puccinia}$ causes rust disease (e.g., wheat rust, $\textit{Puccinia graminis}$), and $\textit{Ustilago}$ causes smut disease (e.g., loose smut of wheat, $\textit{Ustilago nuda}$). Both belong to Class Basidiomycetes. Option B presents rust and smut in the exact order requested.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Plant viruses usually have single-stranded RNA, whereas bacteriophages usually possess double-stranded DNA.
Reason (R): Genetic material in viruses can never be both RNA and DNA simultaneously within the same viral capsid.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
B) Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A).
C) (A) is true but (R) is false.
D) (A) is false but (R) is true.
questions.explanation: Both statements are correct facts from NCERT. Assertion (A) accurately describes the typical genome structures: plant viruses generally contain ssRNA (e.g., TMV), while bacteriophages contain dsDNA (e.g., T4 phage). Reason (R) is also true: no virus possesses both RNA and DNA in its nucleoprotein core. However, the universal exclusivity of nucleic acid types (R) does not explain *why* plant viruses specifically contain single-stranded RNA while phages contain double-stranded DNA (which relates to host cell machinery evolution and replication mechanics). Therefore, both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.questionText: In the mutualistic lichen symbiosis, what specific physiological role does the mycobiont perform for the benefit of the phycobiont?
options: A) Carries out oxygenic photosynthesis to synthesize carbohydrates
B) Directly synthesizes vitamins and ATP via cyclic photophosphorylation
C) Provides structural anchorage, shelter, and absorbs water and mineral nutrients from the substrate
D) Produces motile gametes for sexual dissemination of the algal partner
questions.explanation: In a lichen, the fungal partner (mycobiont) provides structural framework, physical shelter, protective shielding from desiccation, and absorbs water and essential mineral nutrients from the substratum, delivering them to the autotrophic algal partner (phycobiont), which synthesizes food by photosynthesis.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.questionText: The parasitic fungus $\textit{Albugo candida}$, which produces white rust on the leaves of mustard, is taxonomically classified under:
questions.explanation: $\textit{Albugo candida}$ is an obligate plant parasite causing white rust of crucifers (mustard). It possesses an aseptate, coenocytic mycelium and reproduces by motile biflagellate zoospores and oogamous sexual reproduction, classifying it within Phycomycetes (Oomycota).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.questionText: Which of the following genera of fungi belongs to the Deuteromycetes and is widely recognized for producing conidial spores that decompose leaf litter and aid in soil mineral cycling?
questions.explanation: $\textit{Trichoderma}$, $\textit{Alternaria}$, and $\textit{Colletotrichum}$ are representative Deuteromycetes highlighted in NCERT. They are predominantly saprophytes or decomposers of organic litter, playing vital roles in soil mineral recycling. $\textit{Rhizopus}$ is a Phycomycete, $\textit{Claviceps}$ is an Ascomycete, and $\textit{Agaricus}$ is a Basidiomycete.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.questionText:
Consider the comparative characteristics of Whittaker's Five Kingdoms (Table 2.1 in NCERT). Examine the following five statements:
(1) Kingdom Monera is the only kingdom containing prokaryotic organisms lacking a nuclear envelope.
(2) Kingdom Protista encompasses organisms with eukaryotic cellular organization, some possessing cell walls while others completely lack cell walls.
(3) Kingdom Fungi possesses a cellulosic cell wall and exhibits purely autotrophic absorptive nutrition.
(4) Animalia is distinguished from all other eukaryotic kingdoms by the complete absence of a cell wall across all developmental stages.
(5) Nuclear membrane is present in members of Protista, Fungi, Plantae, and Animalia.

How many of the above statements are strictly CORRECT?
questions.explanation: Let us evaluate each statement based on NCERT Table 2.1: (1) Correct: Monera is the sole prokaryotic kingdom lacking a nuclear envelope. (2) Correct: Protista members are eukaryotic; chrysophytes and dinoflagellates have cell walls, whereas euglenoids and protozoans lack cell walls. (3) INCORRECT: Fungal cell walls are composed of chitin and polysaccharides (NOT cellulose), and fungi are exclusively heterotrophic (absorptive), never autotrophic. (4) Correct: All animals are multicellular eukaryotes completely lacking cell walls. (5) Correct: All four eukaryotic kingdoms (Protista, Fungi, Plantae, Animalia) possess a well-defined nuclear membrane. Therefore, four statements (1, 2, 4, 5) are correct (count = 4). Option C is correct.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Penicillin, a beta-lactam antibiotic that inhibits peptidoglycan cell wall cross-linking, is completely ineffective against $\textit{Mycoplasma}$ infections.
Reason (R): $\textit{Mycoplasma}$ organisms are pleomorphic prokaryotes that completely lack a cell wall.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: A) (A) is true but (R) is false.
B) Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A).
C) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
D) (A) is false but (R) is true.
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is true: penicillin acts by inhibiting the transpeptidase enzyme responsible for cross-linking peptidoglycan polymers during bacterial cell wall synthesis. Reason (R) is true: $\textit{Mycoplasma}$ naturally lacks any peptidoglycan or cell wall architecture (surrounded only by a trilaminar lipoprotein membrane). Because there is no cell wall target for penicillin to disrupt, $\textit{Mycoplasma}$ is intrinsically insensitive to beta-lactam antibiotics. Thus (R) provides the exact pharmacological and biological explanation for (A).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.questionText: Which of the following comparisons between Ascomycetes and Basidiomycetes is biologically and cytologically ACCURATE?
options: A) Ascomycetes produce 4 ascospores exogenously, whereas Basidiomycetes produce 8 basidiospores endogenously.
B) Basidiomycetes possess coenocytic aseptate hyphae, whereas Ascomycetes possess branched septate hyphae.
C) In both classes, asexual conidiospores are the dominant mode of reproduction in natural populations.
D) Ascomycetes produce 8 ascospores endogenously inside an ascus, whereas Basidiomycetes produce 4 basidiospores exogenously on a basidium.
questions.explanation: In Ascomycetes, karyogamy and meiosis inside the ascus mother cell followed by a post-meiotic mitotic division yield 8 haploid ascospores borne endogenously inside the ascus. In Basidiomycetes, karyogamy and meiosis inside the basidium yield 4 haploid basidiospores produced exogenously on sterigmata at the tip of the basidium. Both classes have branched, septate hyphae. Option B is strictly accurate.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.questionText:
Examine the following statements regarding the dynamic life cycle of acellular slime moulds:
Statement I: Under favorable environmental conditions, slime moulds differentiate to form fruiting bodies that bear spores at their tips.
Statement II: During unfavorable conditions, the plasmodium differentiates to form fruiting bodies bearing spores that survive for years due to true resistant cell walls.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
B) Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
C) Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
D) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
questions.explanation: Statement I is incorrect: under favorable conditions, slime moulds aggregate into a vegetative, amoeboid multinucleate mass called a plasmodium (they do not form fruiting bodies in favorable conditions). Statement II is correct: when conditions become unfavorable (drought, food shortage), the plasmodium differentiates and produces stalked fruiting bodies bearing spores at their tips; these spores have true cellulosic walls that confer extreme resistance. Thus Statement I is incorrect and Statement II is correct.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Cyanobacteria, despite lacking membrane-bound chloroplasts, are capable of carrying out oxygenic photosynthesis with water as an electron donor.
Reason (R): Cyanobacteria possess lamellar thylakoids distributed freely in their peripheral cytoplasm containing chlorophyll a and phycobiliproteins.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A).
B) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
C) (A) is true but (R) is false.
D) (A) is false but (R) is true.
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is true: cyanobacteria are prokaryotes and therefore lack membrane-bound plastids or chloroplasts, yet they carry out true oxygenic photosynthesis identical to higher plants. Reason (R) is true: they contain flattened, unstacked photosynthetic thylakoid membranes in their chromoplasm (peripheral cytoplasm) embedded with chlorophyll a and light-harvesting phycobilisomes. These cytoplasmic thylakoids perform light absorption and photolysis of water. Thus (R) correctly explains how they achieve oxygenic photosynthesis without chloroplasts.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.questionText:
Consider the following five fungal taxa:
(1) $\textit{Rhizopus stolonifer}$
(2) $\textit{Penicillium notatum}$
(3) $\textit{Ustilago nuda}$
(4) $\textit{Alternaria solani}$
(5) $\textit{Agaricus bisporus}$

Which of the following correctly groups these fungi according to their presence of a distinct dikaryotic phase ($n+n$) during their sexual cycle?
options: A) Dikaryotic phase present: (1) and (4); Dikaryotic phase absent: (2), (3), and (5)
B) Dikaryotic phase present: (1), (2), and (3); Dikaryotic phase absent: (4) and (5)
C) Dikaryotic phase present: (2), (3), and (5); Dikaryotic phase absent: (1) and (4)
D) Dikaryotic phase present in all five taxa
questions.explanation: A prolonged dikaryotic phase ($n+n$) is a distinctive cytological feature occurring in Ascomycetes and Basidiomycetes, where plasmogamy is not immediately followed by karyogamy. (2) $\textit{Penicillium}$ is an Ascomycete, and (3) $\textit{Ustilago}$ and (5) $\textit{Agaricus}$ are Basidiomycetes; hence all three display a dikaryon stage. In contrast, (1) $\textit{Rhizopus}$ is a Phycomycete where plasmogamy leads directly to karyogamy forming a diploid zygospore ($2n$), and (4) $\textit{Alternaria}$ is a Deuteromycete lacking sexual reproduction altogether. Therefore, Option B correctly classifies them.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.questionText:
An infectious sub-viral agent $Z$ was isolated from diseased crop plants. Biochemical assays revealed:
(i) It consists exclusively of single-stranded, circular RNA.
(ii) Treatment with proteases and nucleases showed that it is resistant to proteases but completely digested by ribonucleases.
(iii) It has an exceptionally low molecular weight and lacks any capsomeric protein coat.
Agent $Z$ is most likely:
questions.explanation: The features described—free infectious RNA of low molecular weight, complete absence of a protein coat, sensitivity to RNases, and resistance to proteases—are the defining criteria of viroids, discovered by T.O. Diener (1971) as the causal agent of potato spindle tuber disease. TMV and T4 phage have protein coats; prions consist purely of protein without any RNA.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Dinoflagellates possess two flagella: one lies longitudinally and the other lies transversely in a furrow between the wall plates.
Statement II: Diatoms possess two flagella of unequal length inserted at the anterior apex of the frustule.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
B) Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
C) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
D) Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
questions.explanation: Statement I is correct: dinoflagellates typically possess two flagella—one oriented longitudinally in a sulcus and the other oriented transversely in an equatorial cingulum (furrow), producing a characteristic spinning locomotion. Statement II is incorrect: diatoms are non-flagellated in their vegetative phase and float passively in water currents; flagella are observed only in the male gametes of centric diatoms, not on the vegetative frustule. Thus Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.questionText:
Match the microbial organisms in Column I with their taxonomic groups and key features in Column II:

Column I: (a) $\textit{Nostoc}$, (b) $\textit{Entamoeba}$, (c) $\textit{Trypanosoma}$, (d) $\textit{Paramecium}$
Column II:
(i) Flagellated protozoan causing African sleeping sickness
(ii) Ciliated protozoan with nuclear dualism (macronucleus and micronucleus) and gullet
(iii) Cyanobacterium with heterocysts performing oxygenic photosynthesis
(iv) Amoeboid protozoan using pseudopodia, parasite causing amoebic dysentery

Select the correct matching combination:
questions.explanation: $\textit{Nostoc}$ is a nitrogen-fixing cyanobacterium with heterocysts (a-iii); $\textit{Entamoeba}$ is an amoeboid protozoan causing amoebiasis/dysentery (b-iv); $\textit{Trypanosoma}$ is a flagellated parasitic protozoan transmitted by tsetse flies causing sleeping sickness (c-i); $\textit{Paramecium}$ is a ciliated protozoan possessing a cytopharynx (gullet) and nuclear dualism (d-ii). Correct matching is (a)-(iii), (b)-(iv), (c)-(i), (d)-(ii).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Deuteromycetes are considered an artificial taxonomic assemblage of fungi rather than a true phylogenetic class.
Reason (R): When sexual reproductive stages are discovered in members of Deuteromycetes, they are transferred into either Ascomycetes or Basidiomycetes based on their sexual morphology.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: A) (A) is true but (R) is false.
B) Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A).
C) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
D) (A) is false but (R) is true.
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is true: Deuteromycetes ('Fungi Imperfecti') is a form-class or artificial grouping created for convenience to house fungi in which sexual reproduction has not been observed. Reason (R) is true: as soon as the sexual (teleomorph) state of a deuteromycete fungus is discovered, it is reclassified into its natural phylogenetic class—most commonly Ascomycetes (if it produces asci) or Basidiomycetes (if it produces basidia). Because members do not share a common sexual phylogenetic origin and are merely placed there temporarily awaiting teleomorph discovery, Deuteromycetes is an artificial taxon. Thus (R) correctly explains (A).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.questionText:
Consider the following four biological entities: (I) Bacteriophage, (II) Viroid, (III) Prion, (IV) $\textit{Mycoplasma}$.
Which of these entities contain BOTH nucleic acid (genetic material) AND protein in their molecular composition?
questions.explanation: Let us examine each entity: (I) Bacteriophage is a virus composed of a DNA genome encapsulated by a protein capsid (contains nucleic acid + protein). (II) Viroid consists purely of naked low molecular weight RNA and completely lacks a protein coat (no protein). (III) Prion consists exclusively of abnormally folded infectious protein and lacks any nucleic acid (no nucleic acid). (IV) $\textit{Mycoplasma}$ is a living bacterium possessing a DNA/RNA genome, ribosomes, enzymes, and membrane proteins (contains nucleic acid + protein). Therefore, only (I) and (IV) possess both nucleic acid and protein. Option A is correct.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.questionText: Which of the following statements regarding the structural organisation and nutritional modes of archaebacteria is INCORRECT?
options: A) Methanogens are obligate aerobes that oxidize methane to produce carbon dioxide and water in ruminant rumens.
B) Halophiles survive in high salt concentrations through bacteriorhodopsin-mediated non-photosynthetic ATP generation.
C) Thermoacidophiles thrive in hot springs at acidic pH ($1-2$) by oxidizing sulfur to sulfuric acid under aerobic conditions.
D) The cell wall of archaebacteria lacks peptidoglycan and is instead composed of pseudomurein or complex glycoproteins.
questions.explanation: Option B is incorrect: methanogens are obligate anaerobes (strictly inhibited or killed by oxygen), not aerobes! They reduce $\text{CO}_2$ or formate using $\text{H}_2$ to generate methane ($\text{CH}_4$), not oxidize methane. Options A, C, and D are scientifically accurate descriptions of archaebacterial physiology.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The boundaries of the Kingdom Protista are not well-defined because what may be 'a photosynthetic protist' to one biologist may be 'a plant' to another.
Statement II: Protistan cell bodies contain a well-defined nucleus and other membrane-bound organelles, and some possess flagella or cilia.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
B) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
C) Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
D) Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
questions.explanation: Both Statement I and Statement II are verbatim statements from NCERT Chapter 2. Statement I is true: the boundaries of Protista are fluid and overlapping (e.g., photosynthetic dinoflagellates and euglenoids have historically been treated by phycologists as algae/plants and by protozoologists as animals). Statement II is true: being eukaryotes, protists possess distinct membrane-bound nuclei, mitochondria, plastids, and complex $9+2$ axonemal flagella/cilia. Both statements are correct.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.questionText: In a laboratory experiment, a suspension containing three plant pathogens—a bacterium ($\textit{Xanthomonas}$), a fungus ($\textit{Albugo}$), and a virus (TMV)—is passed through a sterile Chamberland porcelain filter with an average pore size of $0.2\;\mu\text{m}$. Which of the three organisms will be detected in the sterile filtrate?
options: D) All three organisms will pass through into the filtrate
questions.explanation: Chamberland porcelain filters (bacteria-proof filters) have pore sizes around $0.1-0.2\;\mu\text{m}$, which retain bacteria ($\textit{Xanthomonas}$, typically $1-2\;\mu\text{m}$) and fungal spores/hyphae ($\textit{Albugo}$, $>5\;\mu\text{m}$). As discovered by Dmitri Ivanowsky in 1892, viruses are ultramicroscopic ($20-300\;\text{nm}$; TMV is $300\;\text{nm} \times 18\;\text{nm}$) and pass freely through bacteria-proof filters into the filtrate. Therefore, only TMV will be present in the filtrate. Option C is correct.
